Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Corporation Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Davies, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech Corporation’s Third Quarter Earnings Call. Joining me today are Robert Thompson, CEO; Susan Miller, CFO; and David Chen, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Robert Thompson.

Robert Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

We made strong progress this quarter. As previously communicated, strategic capital allocation remains a top priority for the company. For the full year 2024, we are revising our cash-based CapEx guidance downward to $3.0 billion, representing a 9.1% reduction from our initial guidance of $3.3 billion provided during the Q4 2023 earnings call. This adjustment reflects a combination of factors including project optimization, efficiency gains in execution, and a strategic reallocation of resources towards higher-ROI initiatives. While we are reducing overall spend, we remain committed to investing in the critical infrastructure and technology required to support our long-term growth objectives. This downward revision to our CapEx guidance reflects our commitment to financial discipline and our ability to optimize our operations. We are confident that these adjustments will not impact our ability to achieve our strategic objectives and deliver strong financial performance. We believe that this approach creates a more sustainable and efficient model for long-term growth.

We also saw great momentum in our Singapore fab expansion project, a critical component of our long-term growth strategy. As previously communicated, this expansion is focused on bolstering our capacity for advanced logic and specialty memory solutions, particularly catering to the burgeoning demand in the AI, automotive, and IoT sectors. As the summary indicated, the Singapore fab expansion is nearing completion. We are pleased to report that construction is approximately 95% complete as of the end of this quarter. The structural build-out, including cleanroom construction across all four phases, is finalized. We successfully achieved groundbreaking in Q1 2023, and we are on track for initial production runs to commence in Q1 of next year.

These achievements underscore our commitment to disciplined execution and innovation.

Now I’ll pass it to Susan Miller to walk through in more detail.

Susan Miller, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

Let me take you through the financials:

First, building on what Robert said, we’ve continued to drive improvements with the Singapore Fab Expansion Project. We project that the Singapore fab will increase our overall manufacturing capacity by approximately 20% once fully operational by the end of 2025. This additional capacity is critical to meeting the growing demand for our advanced semiconductor solutions. We anticipate a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion with initial production from the Fab. The Singapore fab is designed to be highly efficient, incorporating advanced automation and process control technologies. We expect this to lead to a reduction in manufacturing costs per wafer, contributing to a projected 2-3 percentage point improvement in our gross margin by the end of 2026. We anticipate the Singapore fab to create approximately 1,500 high-skilled jobs in engineering, manufacturing, and support functions. We are actively partnering with local universities and vocational schools to develop training programs and ensure a pipeline of qualified talent.

We invested strategically in capital expenditures this area, resulting in a $300 million reduction in our CapEx budget. This can be attributed to the following key adjustments: Data Center Optimization & Efficiency Gains, resulting in a reduction of $120 million, where our ongoing efforts to enhance the efficiency of our existing data center infrastructure are yielding significant cost savings. We’ve implemented advanced cooling technologies, optimized server utilization through virtualization, and consolidated redundant systems. These initiatives, combined with strategic colocation agreements in the Asia-Pacific region, have allowed us to defer some planned data center expansion projects. Specifically, the planned expansion of our Singapore data center, initially budgeted at $80 million for 2024, has been pushed to early 2025 after a thorough review of current capacity and projected demand. Furthermore, efficiency gains across our North American data centers have freed up capacity, resulting in a further $40 million reduction in planned upgrades. Supply Chain Efficiencies & Negotiated Vendor Agreements, resulting in savings of $80 million, where our procurement team has successfully negotiated more favorable terms with key suppliers of networking equipment, servers, and other essential infrastructure components. The shift towards a more diversified supplier base, particularly in the memory and storage segments, has also contributed to cost reductions. We anticipate these savings to be sustainable throughout the year and potentially extend into future years. For example, renegotiated contracts with server vendors resulted in an average price reduction of 7% per unit compared to the original budget assumptions. Strategic Prioritization of Cloud Infrastructure Investments, resulting in savings of $50 million, where while we remain committed to our hybrid cloud strategy, we are strategically prioritizing investments in public cloud infrastructure over on-premise solutions in certain areas. This shift is driven by the scalability, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness of cloud services, particularly for applications with fluctuating demand patterns. This re-prioritization mainly affects our European expansion plans where we are leveraging existing cloud infrastructure to support growth rather than building out our own facilities. Deferred Non-Critical Infrastructure Projects, resulting in savings of $50 million, where after careful review, we have deferred several non-critical infrastructure projects that were originally planned for 2024. These projects, while beneficial, are not essential to supporting our core business operations or strategic growth initiatives in the near term. Examples include upgrades to office infrastructure that are not immediately required and can be postponed without impacting employee productivity. For Q1 2024, our cash-based CapEx was $650 million, slightly below our initial projection of $700 million. This underspend was primarily due to the aforementioned supply chain efficiencies and some minor delays in the deployment of new networking equipment. However, these delays are not expected to impact our overall CapEx spending for the year, as we anticipate catching up in the subsequent quarters. Specifically, in Q1, we continued to invest in expanding our network infrastructure to support growing bandwidth demands, particularly in emerging markets, and our investment in 5G infrastructure in Latin America remains on track. We allocated $100 million in CapEx to enhance our security infrastructure, including upgrades to our firewall systems and the implementation of advanced threat detection technologies. This investment is crucial for protecting our data and systems from increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. We are investing heavily in building out our AI/ML infrastructure to support our research and development efforts in areas such as natural language processing, computer vision, and machine learning. We've seen a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. Investment in APAC remained strong, driven by increased adoption of our cloud services in the region. We are seeing particularly strong growth in India and Southeast Asia. While we are reducing our CapEx spending in 2024, we remain committed to investing in the long-term growth of our business. We anticipate that our CapEx spending will increase in 2025 and beyond as we continue to expand our global footprint, develop new products and services, and invest in emerging technologies. We are constantly evaluating our capital allocation priorities to ensure that we are maximizing the return on our investments and creating value for our shareholders. We anticipate a gradual increase in CapEx over the next 3-5 years, averaging a 5-7% annual growth rate, driven by the aforementioned factors and the need to support our ambitious growth targets. We will continue to provide updates on our CapEx guidance during our quarterly earnings calls.

Additionally, we’ve seen progress in our capacity utilization rate, and we believe that focusing on optimizing our product mix to maximize profitability is key. As previously mentioned, our capacity utilization rate for the third quarter reached 71%, a positive step up from the 68% we recorded in Q2. While this 3 percentage point increase might appear modest at first glance, it reflects significant underlying improvements in operational efficiency and demand management. This uplift contributed directly to a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year, bringing it to $2.3 billion. The utilization rate increase wasn't uniform across all our operating regions. North America saw the most significant gain, jumping from 65% in Q2 to 73% in Q3. This was largely driven by increased demand in the automotive and aerospace sectors, particularly for our high-precision components. Europe, on the other hand, saw a more moderate increase, moving from 69% to 71%, reflecting the ongoing economic uncertainty in the region. Asia-Pacific remained relatively stable at around 70%, although we did observe a slight dip in China due to localized supply chain disruptions. We are actively working on diversifying our supplier base in that region to mitigate future risks. A key contributor to the overall utilization rate improvement was the successful implementation of our "Phoenix Project," a company-wide initiative focused on streamlining production processes and reducing downtime. Specifically, the Phoenix Project involved the deployment of advanced predictive maintenance algorithms across our key manufacturing facilities. This allowed us to anticipate equipment failures and schedule maintenance proactively, resulting in a 10% reduction in unscheduled downtime across our global network. This translates to approximately 50,000 additional production hours compared to the previous quarter. Another important factor was our strategic focus on optimizing our product mix. We consciously shifted production towards higher-margin, higher-demand products, particularly those related to renewable energy infrastructure. Demand for our advanced battery components, for example, surged by 25% in Q3, requiring us to allocate additional capacity to meet this demand. This strategic realignment, while requiring some initial capital investment in retooling, proved to be highly effective in boosting overall utilization and profitability. In addition to operational efficiencies and product mix, our updated pricing strategies introduced in Q2 are starting to show tangible results. By implementing dynamic pricing models that consider real-time demand and capacity constraints, we were able to optimize revenue per unit and incentivize customers to shift their orders to periods of lower utilization. This, in turn, helped to smooth out demand fluctuations and improve overall plant efficiency. Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, we anticipate the capacity utilization rate to be in the high 60% range, specifically between 67% and 69%. Several factors contribute to this slightly more conservative guidance: Historically, Q4 tends to be a slightly weaker quarter for us due to seasonal slowdowns in several key industries, including construction and heavy machinery. We anticipate a decrease in demand from these sectors as winter approaches in the Northern Hemisphere. We have scheduled major maintenance activities at several of our key facilities during Q4. These activities are essential for ensuring the long-term reliability and efficiency of our operations, but they will inevitably impact our utilization rate in the short term. These planned shutdowns will reduce capacity by roughly 8%. As part of our broader strategy to optimize working capital, we are proactively managing our inventory levels. This means reducing production of certain slow-moving items in Q4 to avoid building up excess inventory. Despite the Q4 guidance, our long-term outlook for capacity utilization remains positive. We expect to see continued improvements in utilization rates in 2024 and beyond, driven by several key factors: The demand for renewable energy infrastructure is expected to continue growing rapidly in the coming years, creating significant opportunities for our business. We are actively investing in expanding our capacity to meet this growing demand, particularly in the areas of battery components and solar panel manufacturing. Our new facility in Nevada, scheduled to come online in Q2 2024, will add significant capacity and is expected to operate at close to full utilization within its first year. We are actively evaluating potential acquisition targets that could further enhance our capacity and capabilities. We are particularly interested in companies that have complementary technologies or access to new markets. We have allocated $500 million for strategic acquisitions over the next 18 months. We are making significant investments in automation and artificial intelligence to further improve our operational efficiency. These investments will enable us to reduce labor costs, increase throughput, and improve the overall utilization of our existing assets. We expect these initiatives to increase our utilization rate by 2-3% by the end of 2024.

Now I’ll turn it over to David, who will speak about operations and innovation.

David Chen, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

Let me begin with a closer look at the revised CapEx guidance, particularly on the regional commentary. Investment in APAC remained strong, driven by increased adoption of our cloud services in the region. We are seeing particularly strong growth in India and Southeast Asia.

I’d also like to expand on our sales guidance, forecast, and trends by segment. While we anticipate a mixed performance across our business segments in Q4, we are cautiously optimistic that strategic initiatives implemented throughout the year will help mitigate some of the broader macroeconomic pressures we are observing. We project overall revenue to be approximately $12.7 billion, representing a slight decline of 2% year-over-year compared to Q4 of the previous fiscal year, which saw revenues of $12.96 billion. This decline is primarily attributable to the strong US dollar and its impact on our reported NT dollar revenue, as well as softening demand in certain consumer-facing segments. The computing segment is expected to show a modest improvement quarter-over-quarter, contributing an estimated $4.8 billion in revenue for Q4. This represents a 3% increase compared to the $4.66 billion reported in Q3. This positive trend is primarily driven by continued strength in the data center market. We're seeing strong demand for our high-performance computing solutions, particularly our next-generation "Archimedes" line of server processors, which offer significant power efficiency and performance gains. We secured a major contract with "Global Cloud Solutions Inc." in Q3, which will begin to contribute significantly to revenue in Q4. Our engagement with AI accelerator manufacturers also continues to drive demand. Furthermore, the refresh cycle in the enterprise server market is providing a tailwind. However, the PC market remains challenged, and we are managing expectations accordingly. We project a 10% increase in Data Center sales in the Computing Segment, but a 6% decrease in PC-related product sales. The communication segment is projected to experience a mild decline in Q4, generating approximately $3.9 billion in revenue, a decrease of 4% compared to $4.06 billion in Q3. This decline is primarily attributed to inventory corrections among our major smartphone OEM customers. After a strong first half of the year fueled by 5G infrastructure buildout and robust smartphone sales, several of our key clients are reporting slower consumer demand and are adjusting their component orders accordingly. We expect this inventory correction to be temporary, with a rebound in Q1 of the next fiscal year as new flagship smartphone models are launched. While we are seeing some positive momentum in the industrial IoT sector, with demand for our embedded communication solutions growing, it's not enough to fully offset the slowdown in the smartphone market. We are prioritizing design wins for next-generation 6G infrastructure to capitalize on future growth opportunities. We anticipate that this segment will stabilize through the second half of next year. The consumer segment is expected to experience a more pronounced decline, with revenue projected at $2.8 billion, a 7% decrease compared to $3.01 billion in Q3. This reflects the broader macroeconomic pressures impacting consumer spending, particularly in discretionary categories like gaming consoles and high-end consumer electronics. Inflationary pressures and rising interest rates are impacting consumer purchasing power, leading to lower demand for these products. We are actively managing our cost structure in this segment and focusing on higher-margin products to mitigate the impact of the revenue decline. We have seen some success with our new line of premium audio products, but this has not been enough to offset the broader slowdown. We are also monitoring the impact of geopolitical tensions on consumer demand in key regions. Wafer shipments are expected to remain relatively flat in Q4 compared to Q3. We are operating our fabrication facilities at near-full capacity, focusing on optimizing our product mix to maximize profitability. The flat wafer shipment volume reflects our strategy of prioritizing higher-value products and managing our inventory levels effectively. We are continuing to invest in expanding our manufacturing capacity to meet future demand, particularly in advanced process technologies. The anticipated appreciation of the NT dollar against the US dollar is expected to negatively impact our reported Q4 NT dollar revenue. We estimate that this currency impact will reduce our reported revenue by approximately 2-3%. We are actively managing our currency exposure through hedging strategies to mitigate the impact of these fluctuations, but some impact is unavoidable. Despite the challenges, we remain confident in our long-term growth prospects. We are continuing to invest in research and development, focusing on next-generation technologies such as AI, quantum computing, and advanced materials. We believe that these investments will position us for long-term success in a rapidly evolving market. We are targeting a gross margin of 48% for Q4, reflecting our focus on higher-margin products and cost optimization. We are managing our operating expenses carefully, aiming for an operating expense ratio of 22%. We expect capital expenditures to be approximately $1.8 billion in Q4, primarily related to expanding our manufacturing capacity. North America remains strong, driven by data center demand and government infrastructure spending. Europe is showing signs of weakness due to the energy crisis and geopolitical instability. Asia-Pacific is a mixed bag, with continued growth in Southeast Asia offset by slower growth in China. Q4 presents a complex landscape with both opportunities and challenges. While we anticipate a slight overall revenue decline due to macroeconomic headwinds and segment-specific dynamics, we are confident that our strategic initiatives, focus on innovation, and disciplined execution will position us for long-term success. We will continue to monitor the market closely and adjust our strategies as needed to maximize shareholder value. We anticipate providing further updates during our Q4 earnings call.

Let’s move to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
You mentioned strong improvements in the capacity utilization rate. Can you talk more about the competitive landscape affecting utilization rates in the Asian market?

Susan Miller:
The Asian market is indeed competitive, particularly with the rise of domestic manufacturers in China. Our strategy to combat this is threefold. First, we're focusing on producing higher-value, technologically advanced components that are difficult for competitors to replicate. Second, we're building stronger relationships with key customers in the region by offering customized solutions and superior customer service. Third, we are actively exploring joint ventures with local partners to gain access to new markets and distribution channels. While pricing pressure exists, we believe our product differentiation and value-added services will allow us to maintain healthy utilization rates.

Analyst 2:
Can you elaborate on the trajectory of the new Fab construction progress and the tool move-in progress?

David Chen:
Sure. We've made significant strides in tool move-in this quarter. Approximately 75% of the planned equipment has now been installed and is undergoing rigorous calibration and testing. This includes advanced lithography systems from ASML, etching equipment from Lam Research, and deposition tools from Applied Materials. We anticipate completing the tool move-in process by the end of Q4 2024.

Analyst 3:
With regard to the revised CapEx guidance, how does this impact our long-term growth strategy?

Susan Miller:
While we are reducing our CapEx spending in 2024, we remain committed to investing in the long-term growth of our business. We anticipate that our CapEx spending will increase in 2025 and beyond as we continue to expand our global footprint, develop new products and services, and invest in emerging technologies. We are constantly evaluating our capital allocation priorities to ensure that we are maximizing the return on our investments and creating value for our shareholders. We anticipate a gradual increase in CapEx over the next 3-5 years, averaging a 5-7% annual growth rate, driven by the aforementioned factors and the need to support our ambitious growth targets. We will continue to provide updates on our CapEx guidance during our quarterly earnings calls.

Closing

Robert Thompson:
Thank you all for joining us today. We're energized by the momentum we’re seeing and look forward to sharing continued progress next quarter.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
